solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fly away after using this spray?

definitions.text: Fly away after using this spray?

parts.words: Fly away after using this spray?
parts.note: read as 'fly' the insect being sent off: the spray is what you use to drive bugs away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly away' looks like an instruction to take off; here a fly is the insect, and the spray is what makes it leave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an aerosol product sprayed on skin or rooms to keep mosquitoes and other bugs from settling.

clue.text: Bad girl admitting crime, finally banned

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the pair takes a letter inside

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word crime

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: A wayward young woman confesses to an offence and ends up excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by law or rule is not permitted, so banned and unlawful coincide.

clue.text: Composer leaves meal unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A composer walks out of dinner before it is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the deletion signal but is only a link; 'unfinished' does the cutting. Franz von Suppé was a 19th-century Austrian composer of light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppé wrote operettas and overtures such as Light Cavalry and Poet and Peasant.

clue.text: Church article samples particular buildings for worship

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
samples as a verb means tries, as in tries food

explanation.surface: A church tries out some article while comparing different places of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantries were chapels endowed so that priests would sing masses for the soul of the founder, a specific kind of religious building.

clue.text: Participant in match, heading off for journey

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a match is a marriage, and a bride takes part in one

explanation.surface: A player in a game sets off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport, but here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a trip on a horse or in a vehicle, a short journey.

clue.text: Fatter as a result of beer — pounds one's hiding

indicators.note: hiding here means the beer conceals the next letters inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Drinking beer has put weight on someone, and they are concealing the money it cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout or rotund, so its comparative describes someone heavier.

clue.text: Pass or failure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to elapse or run out
second meaning: a slip or failing

explanation.walkthrough: Pass and failure look like opposite exam results; the answer covers both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used for time passing or a policy expiring, and for a momentary slip in judgement or concentration.

clue.text: Ensure no hint of tittle-tattle spreading!

definitions.text: Ensure no hint of tittle-tattle spreading!

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters being scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is T

explanation.surface: A warning to keep a secret from becoming gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the French phrase is said when telling a secret that must go no further.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'between ourselves', a confidential aside that should not be repeated.

clue.text: Happen to be in crowd at game?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ..., as in it turned out to be true
second meaning: the number of spectators who attend

explanation.walkthrough: As a phrasal verb the answer means 'prove to be'; as one word it is the attendance figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The attendance at a sporting event is called the turnout, and 'turn out' means prove or happen to be.

clue.text: Native of cold territory, one descending, having crossed mountain to the west

indicators.note: crossed here means the outer word spans the inner one, taking it inside

parts.note: a lander is a craft that descends to a planet's surface

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: An Arctic native comes down from a height after traversing a peak westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, westward is right to left, so the mountain is read backwards before being taken inside the descending craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the Arctic region of northern Scandinavia and Finland, and its inhabitants are called by this name.

clue.text: Victorian essayist's half-hearted idle chat?

indicators.note: the word has a doubled heart, and losing half of it removes one of the two middle letters

parts.note: patter is glib or idle talk

explanation.surface: A Victorian writer's chatter was rather lacking in enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the chat word is its double T; half of it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Pater was a Victorian critic and essayist, author of Studies in the History of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Speculate about time these folk may arrive for dinner

definitions.text: these folk may arrive for dinner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verb goes round the letter

parts.note: to guess is to speculate

explanation.surface: A host wonders roughly when the dinner visitors will turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: People invited to a meal are visitors, the ones who come to the table at a host's invitation.

clue.text: Change, say, when meeting old, trusted friend

parts.note: to alter is to change
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Something shifts when you meet up with a long-standing confidant.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is also used for a very close and intimate companion.

clue.text: See a hundred relations making time for private drink

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Visiting a crowd of relatives prompts someone to arrange a quiet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lock-in is when a pub locks its doors at closing time but lets regulars keep drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a session after official closing hours when the publican keeps serving behind locked doors, an informal period of drinking.

clue.text: Explorer gets cold thigh going over steppe maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means being placed above what follows

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ham is the back of the thigh, or the thigh of a pig
a steppe is an example of a plain, a flat grassland

explanation.surface: An explorer with a chilly leg crosses a grassy plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel de Champlain was the French navigator who founded Quebec, giving his name to Lake Champlain.

clue.text: Behind river, exposed fish

parts.note: a seat is a person's behind or bottom
R is the abbreviation for river on maps
out means revealed, as a secret is out

explanation.surface: Someone sits behind a river and a fish is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a migratory form of brown trout that lives in the sea and runs up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: AA might be travelling around country

indicators.note: travelling around suggests the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation, may be touring a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African nation along the Gambia river, one of few with 'The' in its official name.

clue.text: Explain tricks, having got honest

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
true means faithful or honest

explanation.surface: Someone explains their deceptions now that they have gone straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or put a meaning on words, a way of explaining them.

clue.text: Suddenly gets angry in front of sexy picture

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece comes before the second in an across answer

parts.note: someone who snaps loses their temper suddenly
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: Someone flares up on seeing a racy photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, a casual picture.

clue.text: Thus top politician conveys his dishonest argument

parts.note: so means thus or therefore

indicators.note: conveys means carries, so the abbreviation holds the next word inside it

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the top politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: So it is that the Prime Minister puts across his deceitful case.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophism is a plausible but fallacious line of reasoning meant to deceive.

clue.text: David's father's making straps for falconers

parts.note: Jesse was the father of King David in the Bible
the possessive ending supplies an S

explanation.surface: King David's father is crafting leather straps used in hawking.
explanation.walkthrough: Jesse's simply becomes the plural noun by dropping the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesses are short leather thongs attached to a hawk's legs, which a falconer holds.

clue.text: More than one flier cries with energy in decline

indicators.note: in a down entry, a decline means sliding lower, so the letter moves down a place

parts.note: shrieks are shrill cries
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Birds' cries become more energetic as they fall away.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of SHRIEKS slips one place down to sit after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrikes are songbirds, also called butcher-birds, so several of them are a group of birds.

clue.text: Roman Catholic father starting register

indicators.note: starting means the first piece begins the second, standing at its front

parts.note: papa is an informal word for father
a list is a register or roll

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest begins a parish register.
explanation.definitionFit: A papalist is a supporter of the papacy, so the word is used for a Roman Catholic.

clue.text: Get lost regularly going round that French city

indicators.note: going round means these letters surround the next ones
regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: its alternate letters are L and S
yon is an old word meaning that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: Telling someone to get lost on a regular basis as they circle a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' only links; the alternate letters come from 'lost'. Lyons is the traditional English spelling of Lyon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is France's third-largest city, on the Rhône and Saône rivers.

clue.text: Comedian gets someone to attract punters to show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ronnie ..., the British comic of The Two Ronnies and Porridge

definitions.text: someone to attract punters to show
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person outside a fair or show who shouts to draw in customers

explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Barker was a much-loved British TV comedian; a barker is a fairground tout.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous comic and the word for a crier who calls in passing customers to an attraction.

clue.text: Lazy type's beginning to change, making money

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is to change, its first letter swapped for another

parts.note: a drone is an idler; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An idler is starting to turn over a new leaf and earn some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new first letter; the definition settles it, since swapping D for K gives a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency unit of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Fast runner briefly interrupted by a fog

indicators.note: interrupted by means the shortened word is broken by a letter inside it
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a hare is a fast-running animal

explanation.surface: A sprinter's run is cut short by a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A haar is a cold sea mist on the east coasts of Scotland and England.

clue.text: One party has a grip on my part of America

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: has a grip on means holding something inside, so the party word wraps round the exclamation

parts.note: a do is a party
ah, like my, is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: One political party claims to control part of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics but is a do, a social gathering; 'my' is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Raid, circumventing commercial security device creating obstruction

indicators.note: circumventing means going around, so the raid word surrounds the next

parts.note: to rob is to raid or steal from
an ad is a commercial
a lock is a device for security

explanation.surface: A raid gets round an advert's security device and causes a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barrier set across a road, and figuratively any hindrance.

clue.text: A warmer nest has to be configured to accommodate ten birds

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so the rearranged letters hold the numeral
configured means arranged in a new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A cosier nest must be designed to house ten birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are seabirds of the North Atlantic, named after the Isle of Man where they once bred in large colonies.
